questions.q: In one sentence, what does Matillion do?
options: It builds the charts and dashboards your team reads
It loads data into a cloud warehouse, reshapes it there and schedules the jobs
It is a database that stores your company's records
It watches your servers and alerts you when they go down
questions.explain: Matillion does three jobs on one platform: it loads data, transforms it, and schedules the work. Think of it as the plumbing that gets raw data ready for reports.

questions.q: When Matillion reshapes your data, where does that work happen?
options: On Matillion's own servers, then the result is sent over
Inside the apps the data came from
Inside your cloud data warehouse, as SQL
On the laptop of whoever built the pipeline
questions.explain: The transforms run as SQL inside your warehouse, which is called push-down. So the warehouse does the heavy lifting, and yes, your warehouse bill grows with it.

questions.q: You open Matillion's pricing page to see what Developer, Teams and Scale cost. What do you find?
options: A monthly dollar price for each plan
One flat yearly price for all three plans
A calculator that turns your usage into dollars
Features for each plan, but no dollar prices
questions.explain: You pay in credits, and the page shows no dollar amount for any plan. Matillion also does not publish the price of one credit, so ask for it in writing before you sign.

questions.q: Someone forgets to switch off an older Matillion ETL instance over the weekend. What happens?
options: Nothing, because it only bills when it moves data
You still pay, because it bills for time switched on, not work done
Matillion pauses it for you after an hour
The pipelines fail until someone restarts it
questions.explain: Matillion ETL counts credits for every hour the software is on in your cloud account. In the post's example, the same instance cost 3 times as much when left on all month.

questions.q: On the current Maia Foundation platform, which kind of pipeline uses more credits for each hour it runs?
options: Transformation pipelines, which reshape data in the warehouse
Loading pipelines, which copy data in from the source
They cost the same per hour
Neither one, because both are free
questions.explain: A transformation hour costs 3 credits, while a loading hour costs 1. So trimming an hour of transformation saves more than trimming an hour of loading.
